report:
**Conclusion:** The health claim is **true**. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved the Kyleena (levonorgestrel-releasing) intrauterine system (19.5 mg) for the prevention of pregnancy for up to five years.

### Evidence Supporting the Claim
* **FDA Approval:** The FDA approved Kyleena in September 2016 as a long-acting, reversible contraceptive indicated for up to 5 years of use.
* **Clinical Efficacy:** Approval was based on a Phase III clinical trial of 1,452 women aged 18–35. The trial demonstrated high contraceptive efficacy, with a 1-year Pearl Index of 0.16 and a cumulative 5-year pregnancy failure rate of approximately 1.45% (5-year Pearl Index of 0.29).

### Context and Nuance
* **Lower Hormone Dose:** Kyleena releases a lower daily dose of levonorgestrel compared to higher-dose (52 mg) IUDs such as Mirena or Liletta. 
* **Duration Limits:** While 52 mg levonorgestrel IUDs have received FDA approvals for extended use up to 8 years, Kyleena's approval remains capped at 5 years. There is currently no FDA authorization or sufficient clinical data supporting off-label extended use of Kyleena past 5 years; the device should be replaced at 5 years if continued contraception is desired.

### Sources
* FDA Approval History: https://www.drugs.com/history/kyleena.html
* Kyleena Prescribing Information: https://www.drugs.com/pro/kyleena.html
* Kyleena Clinical Trial Efficacy: https://www.kyleenahcp.com/about-kyleena/efficacy
* Planned Parenthood IUD Overview: https://www.plannedparenthood.org/learn/birth-control/iud
